newsitem.title: NIGERIA: World Bank expert urges Nigeria to privatise.
newsitem.headline: World Bank expert urges Nigeria to privatise.

text.p: A senior official of the World Bank on Wednesday advised Nigeria's military government to revive its economy by privatising key sectors.

"The urge for privatisation is so strong...that I think we can expect that this government or the next will have to decide to pursue that course," Thomas Hutcheson, resident economist of the World Bank, told an economic forum in Lagos.
Sectors such as electricity, petroleum, telecommunications and fertiliser distribution needed to be privatised, he said.
Nigeria embarked on the sale of public enterprises in the second half of the 1980s when it implemented a structural adjustment programme (SAP) but has since suspended this.
General Sani Abacha's government, which came to power in 1993, dumped SAP wholesale the following year but since 1995 has being implementing what it terms "guided deregulation."
Hutcheson's suggestion tallies with one made at a major economic forum in Abuja last week by Pascal Dozie, president of the Nigerian Stock Exchange that the government should resume privatisation.
Dozie said this would consolidate the gains made by the gradual deregulation of the economy which has stabilised the exchange rate of Nigeria's naira currency.
"The World Bank believes privatisation is key for partnership with Nigeria," Hutcheson said.
Relations between Nigeria's government and the World Bank have improved since 1994 when the country dumped SAP.

The gradual opening of the economy has been welcomed by the multilateral lending agency, which is urging Nigeria to go a step further and remove caps on interest rate and scrap the dual exchange system, measures many economists believe will be taken in next year's fiscal budget.
Hutcheson said "Our mutual understanding has improved."
